content: In France, prenatal and postnatal medical care is completely funded through the public healthcare system. Working women are eligible for a 16-week maternity leave, with daily payments ranging from €9.29 ($10.94) to €84.90 ($100), depending on prior earnings. Financial challenges surrounding pregnancy and childbirth largely align with individuals’ pre-existing economic situations: struggling families face similar difficulties as before, while affluent families maintain their status. However, when it comes to providing proper support for new mothers, the system falls short. Fathers are allocated only 11 days of leave, insufficient for mothers to recover and adapt to their new roles. Mothers must address the continuous demands of caring for a newborn while also focusing on recovery. They face the challenge of securing childcare, which remains limited as government programs don’t meet the demand, particularly around Paris. Childcare costs vary significantly, with lower-income families potentially spending €1,000 ($1,177.59) annually for daycare, though space is scarce, with only one available spot for every eight children. Many families turn to private caregivers or similar solutions. Any other questions?
